differences.what: Exposure of the white carton body. A renders it as white: the front face runs from 249 to 225 luma top to bottom and the label paper sits near 245. B renders the same carton as light grey: the front face runs from 237 to 199 and the side face from 184 to 152, so the product looks dull and slightly underexposed. Geometry, noise and edges are otherwise identical, because this is one render graded two ways.

Separation between product and backdrop. At the right silhouette the face-to-backdrop step is 118 levels in A (240 against 122) and 99 in B (213 against 114). At the left silhouette it is 72 in A and 59 in B. B's darker backdrop (99 to 115, against 108 to 127 in A) does not make up for its greyer product.
White 'SHAKE WELL' type on the red base. It reads as clean white in A (236 to 242) and as dull grey in B (205 to 214). The red band itself is identical in both, about RGB 141/27/27.

Contrast of the label and logo. In the Nutrition Facts block the ink-to-paper step is 131 levels in A and 109 in B. The paper around the earmilk logo is 249 in A and 236 in B, so A's printed type stands out more crisply. Both share the same softness at small sizes ('Impedance' reads as 'Impodance' in both).

Highlights on the 'OPEN OTHER SIDE' tab. B hard-clips the tab type to pure 255 (293 pixels clipped in all channels) while every other white in B sits 30 to 50 levels lower. That makes the grade's white point inconsistent across the product. A rolls the same type off to 251 with no full clip, and its whites agree with each other: tab 251, body 249, base type 242.

Modelling in the white highlights. A's shoulder flattens the top of the front face into a near-white plateau of 249 to 250 under the eave. Its rounded corner highlight sits only 4 levels above the face (248 against 244), where B's sits 12 levels above (232 against 220). B's front face also keeps a 38-level falloff from top to bottom against A's 24, so B holds more shape in the whites.

Pink-white light bleed where the side face meets the dark-red gable. It is a defect in both images but slightly hotter in A (95th-percentile luma 112 against 105), so it catches the eye a little more there.
